covers: Middleware, canonicalization, auth route guard, public-origin derivation, hidden admin routes, SEO route classification.

order_of_operations: 1. build one URL from getPublicOrigin(request) + pathname + search
5. if any of 2-4 fired: 308 redirect immediately, guard runs on the follow-up request
6. else: check session cookie presence, run guardedRedirect()
middleware.trap_fixed_2026-08-13: previously used url.origin directly, which Next resolves from the server bind address (127.0.0.1:3020 behind nginx in prod), sending prod visitors to https://localhost:3020/... (f009). Also affected src/app/bff/auth/refresh/route.ts (formerly src/app/api/auth/refresh) via the same pattern — fixed with getPublicOrigin() in both places.

priority: PUBLIC_SITE_ORIGIN env var if set and parses
Host header (+ forwarded-proto or scheme inferred from isLocal())
public_origin.local_detection: hostnames localhost/127.0.0.1/0.0.0.0/[::1], private IP ranges 10.x/192.168.x/172.16-31.x, or *.local suffix are treated as http; everything else defaults to https when no proto header present

route_guard.why_exceptions_matter: these sit under a guarded prefix but must stay reachable with an expired/cleared session cookie — payment returns carry their own short-lived pending-payment cookie; /profile/deleted is reached with the session deliberately destroyed post-deletion
route_guard.note: cookie presence is a cheap routing convenience only — every backend call is still independently validated server-side, this is NOT the authorization boundary

routes: /xloginy (purchase/user/OTP admin dashboard, backed by bff/admin/dashboard, bff/admin/login)
/xerrors (sanitized backend error inbox: filter/inspect/resolve/repair, backed by bff/admin/errors/**)
hidden_admin_routes.discoverability: deliberately unlinked from any nav; kept out of crawl/sitemap via privateRoutePrefixes

seo_private_prefixes.effect: Disallow'd in robots.txt and excluded from sitemap.ts; /api kept in the list even though it's served by Express (still non-indexable)

canonical_host: esim.uplisoft.com (apex, not www), enforced by middleware; production Next process binds 127.0.0.1:3020 behind nginx
